title: "G03: Sex hormones and modulators of the genital system"
description: "ATC G03 sex hormones and modulators of the genital system for modelers: you are dosing into a feedback loop; baseline is rhythmic, so sampling time is a covariate; response outlasts exposure."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

Part of [G: Genito-urinary system and sex hormones](../).

**You are dosing into a feedback loop.**
Exogenous hormone suppresses endogenous secretion, so the measured concentration is the drug plus a baseline that moves in response to it [@bi2018tc; @pastuszak2021tu].
Start from turnover (indirect response), not a direct-effect model [@pechstein2000cetrorelix; @snelder2019leuprorelin], and add an explicit feedback term when modeling the axis itself [@tornoe2007hpg] (see [pharmacodynamics](/docs/concepts/pd/)).

**Baseline is rhythmic, so sampling time is a covariate.**
Testosterone follows a circadian rhythm, most pronounced in younger men [@brambilla2009diurnal; @diver2003diurnal]; in premenopausal women LH, FSH, estradiol and progesterone vary across the menstrual cycle [@stricker2006menstrual; @roblitz2013menstrual].
A pre-dose sample drawn at an arbitrary hour is one point on a rhythm, not a baseline [@dansirikul2008baseline; @bhasin2018guideline].

**Response outlasts exposure.**
Steroids act through nuclear receptors and gene transcription [@burris2013nr], so endpoints such as luteinising hormone, spermatogenesis and prostate specific antigen move on the timescale of the affected system, not of plasma concentration [@bi2018tc; @gisleskog1998dht].

**Flip-flop is the norm.**
Depot injections, implants, transdermal systems and vaginal rings make the formulation set the input rate [@francis2021dmpa; @timmer2000nuvaring].
For non-removable depots absorption is slower than elimination, so the apparent terminal half-life belongs to the vehicle [@kuan2023flipflop; @periti2002leuprorelin].

**Mechanistic extrapolation.**
PBPK dominates here, predicting how CYP3A inducers such as efavirenz or rifampicin lower ethinylestradiol and progestin exposure, and whether dose adjustment preserves contraceptive efficacy [@lewisPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2024; @adeojoPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2024].
